claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask a few questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! And the next question:

**Do you live with Alex, or are you responsible for them in another way (such as contributing financially to their upkeep)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has actually been in hospital for a while now - a few months actually. But I still regularly spend money on things for them, like their favorite snacks, magazines, and clothes they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. A few months is significant, so I need to understand this better:

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital? Is it more than 12 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been about 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's helpful to know. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is the hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one more important question:

**Has Alex had any breaks from the hospital during these 15 weeks? For example, has Alex come home for any periods of time during this hospital stay?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they've been in the hospital ward continuously during this time. They haven't been able to come home at all.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also check one final detail:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Even though Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (which is longer than the usual 12-week limit), you qualify for an important exception. Because you regularly spend money on Alex while they're in hospital - buying things like snacks, magazines, and clothes - you can continue to receive Child Benefit beyond the 12-week threshold.

The key factors supporting your eligibility are:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK and Alex normally lives with you
- Alex is in a UK hospital
- You regularly spend money on Alex during their hospital stay
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You should inform HMRC about Alex's hospital stay if you haven't already done so, but based on your circumstances, you should be able to continue receiving Child Benefit.

According to the rules, there is an exception to the 12-week limit for children in a UK hospital if the claimant regularly spends money on them. This exception applies in Alex's case, meaning the claimant can continue to receive Child Benefit despite Alex being in hospital for more than 12 weeks. No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.
